title: Salade niçoise with seared tuna
skill: Four parts, hot and cold, on one timeline

notes.text: Sear the tuna in two batches, and cook the eggs in a wider pot so they sit in one layer.

move.title: One plate, one timeline
move.body: A salade niçoise from Nice is a composed salad: potatoes, green beans, eggs, tomatoes, olives, and tuna, each cooked or cut on its own and arranged, not tossed. This is the unit's mastery week. You'll write a timeline backward from serving and run it, so every part is ready at once.

why.title: Plan backward
why.body: Start from serving time and subtract each part's time. Potatoes take longest, so they start first. Tuna is seared last, because it's best warm and only needs a few minutes.

why.title: One pot, staggered
why.body: The green beans cook in the potatoes' water for the last few minutes. One pot of boiling water does two jobs, and both finish together.

why.title: Ice bath
why.body: Plunging eggs and beans into ice water stops their cooking at once. The beans stay bright and crisp, and the eggs peel cleanly.

why.title: Dress potatoes warm
why.body: Warm potatoes soak up dressing; cold ones only get coated. Toss them as soon as they're drained.

why.title: Tuna to 145°F
why.body: Restaurants often serve tuna rare. This app cooks all fish to 145°F, the safe minimum. A hot pan and a short, hard sear on 1-inch steaks still gives a browned crust, and slicing against the grain keeps it tender.

wrong.sign: Everything was ready except the potatoes
wrong.fix: Start them earlier: they're the longest part. Rewrite the timeline with 5 minutes of slack.

wrong.sign: The green beans are dull and soft
wrong.fix: They cooked too long or missed the ice bath. Next time, 4 minutes, then straight into ice.
Chill them fully in the ice bath and peel under running water, starting at the wide end.
Pull it the moment it reads 145°F; a thicker steak stays moister than a thin one.

quiz.q: Why cook the beans in the potatoes' water?
choices: One pot does two jobs and both finish together
quiz.explain: They go in for the last 4 minutes.

quiz.q: Why dress the potatoes while warm?
What temperature does the tuna need to reach?

steps.text: Write a timeline backward from serving time: potatoes 20 minutes, eggs 12, beans 4, tuna 10 with resting, plating 5.
steps.tip: Add 5 minutes of slack at the start. Run it with your phone's clock.

steps.text: Put the potatoes in the large pot, cover with cold water by 1 inch, add the tablespoon of salt, and bring to a boil.
Simmer until a knife slides in easily.
Fill the large bowl with ice and water.
Bring the saucepan of water to a simmer. Lower in the eggs with the slotted spoon.
Whisk the dressing's olive oil, vinegar, mustard, salt, and pepper in the small bowl.
Move the eggs to the ice bath.
Peel one egg and slide the thermometer sideways into the white. It needs to read at least 160°F; if not, return the rest for 1 minute.
Trim the beans. Add them to the potatoes for the last 4 minutes, then lift them into the ice bath.
Drain the potatoes, halve them, and toss them warm in the medium bowl with 2 tablespoons of dressing.
Pat the tuna dry and season it with the tuna's salt and pepper.
Wash your hands, the board, and the tongs with soap.
Heat the vegetable oil in the skillet over high heat until it smokes. Sear the tuna on each side.
Check the center of the thickest steak. It needs to read at least 145°F; if not, 1 more minute a side.
While the tuna rests 3 minutes, line the plates with lettuce. Arrange the potatoes, beans, tomato wedges, olives, and peeled, halved eggs in groups.
Slice the tuna across the grain and add it. Spoon the rest of the dressing over everything, scatter the capers, and serve.
